---
title: "Model manifest"
---

Every published model ships `ephysatlas_model.json` — the **publication contract**. It is
a discriminated union keyed on `model_class` that normalises every model family into one
shape, which is what lets a single `load_pretrained` call serve them all.

A model directory without a manifest is not loadable. The manifest is also the only record
of settings that cannot be recovered from the weights, such as the spatial encoder's
neighbourhood radius.

ibleatools only ever **reads** this file:
[`read_manifest`](../api/model_registry.read_manifest.qmd) parses it,
[`resolve_model`](../api/model_registry.resolve_model.qmd) fetches the directory, and
[`verify_checksums`](../api/model_registry.verify_checksums.qmd) validates the bytes.

```python
model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost", revision="2026_W42"
)
print(model.index)   # the parsed manifest
```

## Common blocks

Every manifest, regardless of family, carries these.

| key | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_id` | str | Human-readable release id, e.g. `2026_W42_Cosmos_flimsy-thistle-cat` |
| `task` | str | What the model does: `region-classification`, `spatial-encoding`, `unit-encoding`, … |
| `model_class` | str | **The dispatch key.** Selects the wrapper class |
| `vintage` | str | The release this model belongs to |
| `granularity` | str | `channel` or `unit` |
| `method` | str | Model type, e.g. `xgboost`, `transformer`, `hierarchical_gmm` |
| `artifacts` | dict | Role → filename(s), for every published file the loader needs |
| `inputs` | dict | Row identity and required columns |
| `outputs` | dict | What `predict` returns |
| `config` | dict | Family-specific settings |
| `training` | dict | Seed, dataset sizes, training-set hash |
| `environment` | dict | Package versions at training time |

### `model_class` dispatch

`load_pretrained` maps `model_class` to a wrapper 1:1. Each family's trainer writes a
different flavour of name — the encoders and the probe transformer record the bare class
name, the region classifier the fully-qualified XGBoost class:

| `model_class` | wrapper |
|---|---|
| `xgboost.sklearn.XGBClassifier` | [`RegionClassifier`](../api/regionclassifier.RegionClassifier.qmd) |
| `ProbeTransformer` | [`ProbeTransformerClassifier`](../api/models.probe_transformer.ProbeTransformerClassifier.qmd) |
| `NeighborInpaintingModel` | [`SpatialEncoder`](../api/models.encoder_inpainting.SpatialEncoder.qmd) |
| `UnitAutoencoder` | [`UnitEncoder`](../api/models.unit_encoder.UnitEncoder.qmd) |

An unrecognised value raises `ValueError` listing the known ones and suggesting an
upgrade — a model published by a newer ibleatools than yours fails clearly rather than
loading half-correctly.

### `environment`

The versions the model was trained with. This is the reference to compare against when
[`selftest`](../how-to/download-models.qmd) fails. The region decoder `2026_W42`:

```json
{
  "python": "3.12.12",
  "xgboost": "3.4.1",
  "scikit_learn": "1.8.0",
  "numpy": "2.5.4",
  "pandas": "2.3.3",
  "torch": "2.14.1",
  "ephysatlas": "0.9.0",
  "iblatlas": "1.3.0"
}
```

## Region-classification manifests

`task: "region-classification"`, `model_class: "xgboost.sklearn.XGBClassifier"`.

```json
{
  "model_id": "2026_W42_Cosmos_flimsy-thistle-cat",
  "task": "region-classification",
  "model_class": "xgboost.sklearn.XGBClassifier",
  "vintage": "2026_W42",
  "granularity": "channel",
  "method": "xgboost",
  "artifacts": {
    "weights": "model.ubj",
    "folds": ["FOLD00", "FOLD01", "FOLD02", "FOLD03", "FOLD04"],
    "split": "split.json"
  },
  "inputs": {
    "table": "raw_ephys_features_denoised.pqt",
    "index": ["pid", "channel"],
    "features": ["rms_lf", "psd_lfp", "..."],
    "feature_order_sha256": "7493de89a612e7e348ca2f077898dc599603bf1ba6c73803507ffef66c3f23bb"
  },
  "outputs": {
    "kind": "categorical",
    "columns": ["predicted_acronym", "predicted_atlas_id",
                "prediction_probability", "fold_agreement"]
  },
  "config": {
    "classes": [0, 313, 315, 512, 549, 623, 698, 703, 997, 1065, 1089, 1097, 2000],
    "class_acronyms": ["void", "MB", "Isocortex", "CB", "TH", "CNU", "OLF",
                       "CTXsp", "root", "HB", "HPF", "HY", "void_fluid"],
    "region_map": "Cosmos",
    "accuracy": 0.6123792770419426
  }
}
```

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `artifacts.weights` | The all-data model, used by `estimator="global"` |
| `artifacts.folds` | Fold subdirectories under `folds/`, averaged by `estimator="ensemble"` |
| `artifacts.split` | The insertion split used in training |
| `inputs.table` | Which published table the features must come from — **the denoised one** |
| `inputs.features` | The required columns, **in order** (48 for `2026_W42`) |
| `config.classes` | Allen structure ids, index-aligned with `class_acronyms` |
| `config.region_map` | Region ontology of the classes, e.g. `Cosmos` |
| `config.accuracy` | Held-out accuracy at training time |

A fold is loadable when its weights file is present. Folds ship weights only and carry no
manifest of their own, which is why the loader keys on the weights file — that is what
keeps every fold in the ensemble instead of silently dropping some.

### The probe transformer

`task: "region-classification-transformer"`, `model_class: "ProbeTransformer"`. The same
classes and region map, with a whole-probe model per seed instead of folds:

```json
{
  "model_id": "ea-decoder-channel-transformer",
  "task": "region-classification-transformer",
  "model_class": "ProbeTransformer",
  "vintage": "2026_W42",
  "granularity": "channel",
  "artifacts": {
    "weights": "best_model.pt",
    "scaler": "feature_scaler.npz",
    "seeds": ["SEED00", "SEED01", "SEED02", "SEED03", "SEED04"]
  },
  "inputs": {
    "index": ["pid", "channel"],
    "features": ["alpha_mean", "alpha_std", "..."],
    "feature_order_sha256": "49a1fc2d942c7187f1f2b050526e95dc85a91d3e17999d88abbc0b5d86816753",
    "position_column": "axial_um"
  },
  "outputs": {
    "kind": "categorical",
    "columns": ["predicted_acronym", "predicted_atlas_id",
                "prediction_probability", "seed_agreement"]
  },
  "config": {
    "classes": [0, 313, "..."],
    "class_acronyms": ["void", "MB", "..."],
    "region_map": "Cosmos",
    "model_config": {"d_model": 128, "n_heads": 4, "n_transformer_layers": 4,
                     "dropout": 0.3, "n_features": 51, "n_classes": 13}
  }
}
```

`inputs.position_column` is the depth the transformer uses as its positional signal, read
alongside the 51 features. `estimator="ensemble"` averages the seeds; `"global"` uses the
first one.

## Spatial-encoding manifests

`task: "spatial-encoding"`, `model_class: "NeighborInpaintingModel"`.

```json
{
  "model_id": "2026_W42_encoder",
  "task": "spatial-encoding",
  "model_class": "NeighborInpaintingModel",
  "vintage": "2026_W42",
  "granularity": "channel",
  "method": "transformer",
  "artifacts": {
    "weights": "spatial_encoder.pt",
    "context": ["agea_vol_pca.npy", "merfish_vol_pca.npy"],
    "confidence": "confidence_model.pt",
    "neighbor_bank": "neighbor_bank.npz",
    "stats": "preprocessing/channel_stats.npz",
    "split": "split.json",
    "results": ["results/confidence_validation.json", "results/test_r2.json"]
  },
  "inputs": {
    "table": "channels.pqt",
    "index": ["pid", "channel"],
    "columns": ["x", "y", "z"]
  },
  "outputs": {
    "kind": "continuous",
    "columns": ["rms_lf", "psd_delta", "..."],
    "feature_order_sha256": "06be1cc9256bcb6bd85b0b45e9e1769f35ef417bf6ee9f0dc8d5603f947163c6"
  },
  "config": {
    "architecture": {"f_ctx": 100, "f_ephys": 43, "f_out": 43, "d_model": 128,
                     "nhead": 8, "depth": 2, "drop": 0.15, "use_positions": false},
    "neighbourhood": {"radius_um": 500.0, "m_max": 8,
                      "selection": "nearest", "allow_same_probe": false},
    "context": {"n_cell_pcs": 50, "n_gene_pcs": 50, "voxel_um": 200, "sources": {"...": "..."}}
  }
}
```

Note the direction: `inputs.columns` are coordinates and `outputs.columns` are features —
the reverse of the classifier.

**The weights alone are not a usable model.** It also needs the frozen PCA context volumes
and a bank of training-channel features to draw neighbours from, neither of which can be
recomputed downstream:

| role | why it ships |
|---|---|
| `weights` | The encoder itself |
| `context` | Frozen AGEA + MERFISH PCA volumes, sampled at the query coordinates |
| `neighbor_bank` | Real features of training channels, to draw neighbours from |
| `confidence` | The per-probe confidence model |
| `stats` | The training statistics, including the per-feature clipping thresholds |
| `split` | The insertion split used in training |
| `results` | Validation metrics, for the record |

`config.neighbourhood` is not reconstructible from the weights, so the manifest is the only
record of it. `allow_same_probe: false` means neighbours come from *other* probes only,
which keeps a prediction honest for a probe already in the bank.
`architecture.use_positions: false` (from `2026_W39` on) means the model was trained
without the position input; an `ephysatlas` that predates the option cannot load it.

## Unit-encoding manifests

`task: "unit-encoding"`, `model_class: "UnitAutoencoder"`.

```json
{
  "model_id": "2026_W42_unit",
  "task": "unit-encoding",
  "model_class": "UnitAutoencoder",
  "vintage": "2026_W42",
  "granularity": "unit",
  "method": "hierarchical_gmm",
  "artifacts": {
    "autoencoder": "autoencoder.pt",
    "config": "config.json",
    "scaler": "shared_latent_scaler.joblib",
    "types": "types_gmm.joblib",
    "subtypes": "subtypes_gmm.joblib",
    "subtype_parent": "subtype_parent.npy",
    "context_transform": "context_transform.joblib",
    "type_weights": "context_weights_types.pt",
    "subtype_weights": "context_weights_subtypes.pt",
    "members": "members.npz",
    "stats": "preprocessing/unit_stats.npz",
    "split": "split.json",
    "context": ["agea_vol_pca.npy", "merfish_vol_pca.npy"],
    "results": ["results/summary.json"]
  },
  "inputs": {
    "index": ["pid", "cluster"],
    "columns": ["x", "y", "z"],
    "modalities": ["waveform", "acg", "stpc"]
  },
  "outputs": {
    "kind": "continuous",
    "columns": ["depolarisation_slope", "recovery_slope", "..."],
    "feature_order_sha256": "8536d8c5c99959110df046905224cf91de680434287153131d3ba85eaed968af",
    "latent_dim": 60
  },
  "config": {
    "architecture": {"modalities": ["waveform", "acg", "stpc"], "modality_latent_dim": 20,
                     "latent_dim": 60, "n_types": 30, "n_subtypes": 300,
                     "max_subtypes_per_type": 10, "min_units_per_subtype": 20},
    "context": {"n_cell_pcs": 50, "n_gene_pcs": 50,
                "source_model": "int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-channel", "data_vintage": "2026_W41"}
  }
}
```

`inputs.columns` are again coordinates: `predict` maps positions to the expected unit
phenotype, the 10 `outputs.columns`. `inputs.modalities` are what `encode` takes for a
unit. The artifacts split the model into its parts:

- the autoencoder and its latent scaler;
- the type and sub-type mixtures, and the parent type of each sub-type;
- the context networks for the type and sub-type weights;
- the training members each sub-type is read out through.

`config.context.source_model` names the spatial-encoder release whose context volumes the
unit model shares.

## Feature-order digests

Where a manifest carries `feature_order_sha256`, the loader re-hashes the feature list and
compares. A mismatch raises `ValueError`.

This catches a manifest that has been edited or reordered — which would otherwise feed the
model a correctly-named but wrongly-ordered feature matrix and produce plausible,
completely wrong numbers.

```python
import ephysatlas.model_registry as mr

digest = mr.feature_order_sha256(model.inputs["features"])
mr.validate_feature_order(
    model.inputs["features"], model.inputs.get("feature_order_sha256")
)
```

## `checksums.json`

Published alongside the manifest: a per-file digest of everything in the release, verified
on load so a truncated download or a file silently dropped at publish time fails loudly.

Supported hashers are `blake2b`, `md5` and `sha1`.

Files edited on the Hub *after* publication are excluded, so they never cause a spurious
failure: `checksums.json` itself (it cannot cover itself), `README.md` (the model card),
`LICENSE`, `.gitattributes`, and the Hub's `.git/` and `.cache/` trees.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import ephysatlas.model_registry as mr

# missing_ok=False is what load_pretrained uses for a local directory
mr.verify_checksums(Path("/data/models/ea-decoder-2026_W42"), missing_ok=False)
```

## `example/` — the golden files

A release may ship an `example/` directory:

```text
example/
├── features_sample.parquet      a small input the model can run on
└── expected_predictions.parquet the output the publisher got from it
```

The unit encoder ships positions and synthetic units instead
(`positions_sample.parquet`, `units_sample.npz`, `expected_predictions.parquet`,
`expected_latents.npy`), so its self-test covers both `predict` and `encode`.

This is what [`selftest`](../how-to/download-models.qmd) uses, and what makes the tutorial
runnable with no data of your own. `selftest` raises `FileNotFoundError` when a model ships
no `example/` — the probe transformer's `2026_W37` release, for one.

Tolerances differ by family, for a reason:

| family | tolerance | why |
|---|---|---|
| `RegionClassifier` | `rtol=1e-5` | Tree ensembles are near-exactly reproducible |
| `ProbeTransformerClassifier` | `rtol=1e-4`, `atol=1e-5` | float32 network outputs, as below |
| `SpatialEncoder` | `rtol=1e-4`, `atol=1e-5` | float32 transformer outputs genuinely drift ~1e-4 from BLAS and library differences. `atol` guards near-zero outputs, which no relative bound can |
| `UnitEncoder` | `rtol=1e-4`, `atol=1e-5` | float32 network outputs, as above |

All are far tighter than real corruption or a wrong model, which drift by orders of
magnitude more.

## Reading a manifest without loading a model

```python
from pathlib import Path
import ephysatlas.model_registry as mr

manifest = mr.read_manifest(Path("/data/models/ea-decoder-2026_W42"))

# A flattened summary of the common fields
print(mr.meta_from_manifest(manifest))

# Class ids -> acronyms in the manifest's region map
print(mr.class_acronyms(manifest["config"]["classes"],
                        manifest["config"]["region_map"]))
```

`read_manifest` returns `None` when there is no manifest, rather than raising — the
wrappers turn that into an explicit error.
